A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDBE research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical results, pseudocode and proof constructions, including its appendices. Section 6 explicitly leaves empirical performance to future work; no original experimental outcomes are reported.

after.justification: Appendix I and Figure 4 report original simulations comparing MDBE with two BinningUCB baselines, with cumulative dynamic regret averaged over 100 independent runs.

M1.justification: The base MDBE procedure and existing multidimensional adaptation are retained. New Appendix G.2 adds a parameterized Hölder adaptation with different block and replay durations, scheduling probabilities and eviction bias terms, while preserving the hierarchical sampling and elimination scheme.

E1.justification: v2 introduces the paper's first empirical evaluation: a synthetic, piecewise-linear 1-Lipschitz bandit on [0,1] with a moving reward peak. v1 has no evaluated dataset or simulation scenario. The Hölder and multidimensional extensions remain theoretical.

E2.justification: Figure 4 introduces actual comparisons against BinningUCB (naive) and BinningUCB (oracle). v1 discusses UCB and an oracle theoretically but reports no empirical comparison against either baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix I adds a simulation protocol measuring cumulative dynamic regret, with ten reported significant shifts, horizon-based discretization without resets for the naive baseline, and phase-specific discretization and resets for the oracle. The horizon is inconsistent: the text and caption specify 10^6 rounds, but Figure 4's title and axis show 100,000.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests or error analyses. The new simulation is a benchmark comparison, and the new computational-cost analysis is theoretical rather than an additional empirical diagnostic.

E5.justification: v2 introduces empirical uncertainty reporting through 100 independent runs and 95% confidence intervals for mean cumulative dynamic regret in Figure 4. v1 has no corresponding empirical reporting. The confidence-interval construction is not specified.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds the first empirical result curves: the oracle has the lowest plotted regret, MDBE is intermediate, and naive BinningUCB has the highest. These are newly reported results, not improvements over v1 measurements; their intended horizon remains inconsistent between plot and caption.

T1.justification: Appendix G.2 adds a Hölder assumption, a corresponding significant-regret definition, and upper- and lower-bound derivations involving the smoothness parameters. Appendix H adds computational-complexity bounds. Appendix D.2 revises the variance calculation, while the principal Lipschitz theorems and existing multidimensional results remain.

C1.justification: The abstract's central adaptive minimax-optimality claim is retained. Remark 1 adds a claim of joint minimax optimality for Hölder parameters, and the conclusion now includes computational analysis and a synthetic empirical demonstration among the contributions.

C2.justification: v1 leaves computational efficiency and empirical performance unaddressed. v2 provides a specific scalability discussion in Appendix H, reporting O(T^6) time and O(T^4) memory bounds and warning about larger blocks. Appendix I attributes the observed advantage over naive BinningUCB to replay-based adaptation.

D1.justification: Beyond the retained pseudocode, v2 adds an implementation-repository link in Appendix I and the checklist. New Table 2 consolidates proof constants, including an explicit eviction constant c0. These improve access information and parameter documentation, although actual hardware and execution times are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kang et al. (2023a) as earlier non-stationary Lipschitz work and distinguishes its setting and guarantees. This is separate from the retained corruption-bandit paper, now Kang et al. (2023b). Additional citations expand contextual, convex and structured-bandit coverage without replacing the main positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized wording edits, a recommendation-system example, expanded explanatory passages, subdivision of Appendix G, a conference checklist, and relocation of the existing broader-impacts paragraph into the main text.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a narrower conference layout with extensive reflow of text, equations and algorithms. It adds the sampling-tree illustration in Figure 1, the experimental plot in Figure 4 and the constants table, and expands the notation table. The two earlier proof diagrams are retained as Figures 2 and 3.

improvement.justification: v2 improves documentation through an empirical illustration with uncertainty bands, code-access information and explicit scalability discussion. However, Figure 4 conflicts with its caption about the horizon, and Appendix G.2 drops a factor 1/κ when substituting its block length into the block-regret expression, despite claiming optimal κ dependence. These inconsistencies affect the principal new empirical and theoretical support. With the central Lipschitz results largely retained, the net quality effect is uncertain.
